title: Article 107 — Provisions as to introduction and passing of Bills

content.overview: Article 107 provides that a Bill may originate in either House (subject to Money Bill rules under Article 109). A Bill is not deemed passed unless agreed to by both Houses, either without amendment or with amendments agreed to by both. A Bill pending in Parliament does not lapse on prorogation, but a Bill pending in the Lok Sabha (or pending in the Rajya Sabha but not passed by the Lok Sabha) lapses on dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
content.glance: Bills may originate in either House (except Money Bills). Both Houses must agree. Pending Bills: no lapse on prorogation; LS dissolution lapses LS Bills and unpassed RS Bills.
content.study:
Article 107:

(1) Subject to the provisions of Articles 109 and 117 with respect to Money Bills and other financial Bills, a Bill may originate in either House of Parliament.

(2) Subject to Articles 108 and 109, a Bill shall not be deemed to have been passed by the Houses of Parliament unless it has been agreed to by both Houses, either without amendment or with such amendments only as are agreed to by both Houses.

(3) A Bill pending in Parliament shall not lapse by reason of the prorogation of the Houses.

(4) A Bill pending in the House of the People which has not been passed by the House of the People shall lapse on a dissolution of the House of the People.

(5) A Bill pending in the Council of States which has not been passed by the House of the People shall not lapse on a dissolution of the House of the People.

Examination: origin in either House (Money Bills special); agreement of both Houses; prorogation ≠ lapse; dissolution of LS lapses Bills pending in LS and those in RS not yet passed by LS.

sections.heading: Origin and passage
sections.body: Subject to Money Bill / financial Bill rules, a Bill may originate in either House. Passage requires agreement of both Houses (with or without agreed amendments).

sections.heading: Lapse rules
sections.body:
- Prorogation: does not cause a pending Bill to lapse.
- Dissolution of Lok Sabha: Bill pending in LS and not passed by LS lapses; Bill pending in RS but not passed by LS also lapses (Art 107(5) as commonly applied in the dissolution context — verify exact clause operation with text).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain introduction and passing of Bills under Article 107.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 107, subject to the special rules for Money Bills and financial Bills, a Bill may originate in either House. It is not deemed passed unless both Houses agree to it, with or without amendments agreed to by both. A Bill does not lapse on prorogation. On dissolution of the Lok Sabha, a Bill pending in the Lok Sabha and not passed by it lapses; a Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha also does not survive dissolution of the Lok Sabha in the sense provided by the article.

examTips: Either House origin (except Money Bills); both Houses agree; no lapse on prorogation; LS dissolution effects.
